repo_notes.content:
CRITICAL MATHEMATICAL REQUIREMENT: All pages that discuss entropy MUST render the core Shannon entropy formula and related expressions using proper LaTeX math mode ($$ ... $$ for display, $ ... $ for inline). Never write the formula in plain text or ASCII approximations.

The canonical definition (from entropy_feature.md) is:

$$H(f|d) = -\sum_{f \in F} P(f|d) \cdot \log_2 P(f|d)$$

Where:
- $H(f|d)$ is the entropy (in bits) of a datatype form $d$ with respect to phrase function $f$
- $d$ is a specific datatype instance (surface text, morph tag, or lemma)
- $f$ ranges over the set of phrase functions $F$ (Subj, Objc, PreC, Pred, Conj, etc.)
- $P(f|d)$ is the empirical conditional probability observed over the entire N1904-TF corpus

Absolute entropy is stored in millibits: value = round($H \times 1000$) as integer.
Normalized entropy is $H / \log_2(|F|)$ (or the effective support size) scaled to [0,1] and stored as float.

Always show the worked example for the surface form λόγος (N-NSM) with its probability distribution and the resulting ≈0.791 bits / 791 millibits. Prefer the exact symbols and notation used in entropy_feature.md and the production notebook. Use Greek text (λόγος) correctly when illustrating surface forms.

repo_notes.content: This repository is a pure feature-generation ETL pipeline. It does not distribute the final features for end-user consumption; those live in tonyjurg/N1904addons. The six features are: lemma_entr_mbit, morph_entr_mbit, text_entr_mbit, lemma_entr_norm, morph_entr_norm, text_entr_norm. Emphasize the distinction between absolute (millibit integer) and normalized ([0,1] float) representations, and the three linguistic keys (lemma / morph / surface text).

pages.title: Absolute vs. Normalized Entropy (mbit and norm)
pages.purpose: Explain the two output representations produced by the pipeline. Absolute entropy is converted to millibits (H × 1000, rounded to integer) for compact integer storage in Text-Fabric. Normalized entropy scales H by the theoretical maximum (log₂ of the number of possible functions or the effective support) into the unit interval [0,1] and is stored as float. Discuss why both scales are useful and how they appear in the six .tf feature files.

page_notes.content:
Show the conversion formulas with LaTeX:

Absolute (millibits): $\text{mbit} = \operatorname{round}(H \times 1000)$ (integer)

Normalized: $\text{norm} = H / \log_2 N$ (or effective support size) ∈ [0,1] (float)

Mention that the production notebook uses vectorized NumPy operations for both calculations.
